_doc: D250: companions whose arcs react (Ewan's #270 keep 1, from Baldur's Gate 3; issue #283). Each of the sixteen can have an arc: a short personal quest that opens after their chapter one (a lead, once it is found; one walking with the company, once the company has stood on the Tower's floor `opens_floor`), and is told at the fire. Read by src/chronicle/arcs.gd. `stages` in order: `ask` is the journal line, `until` what finishes it (`count` deeds since the stage opened that match any of `deeds`), `skip_if` lets what the company did before the arc opened finish it at once. `opened`, each stage's `done` and `finished` are lines said at the fire: a list of variants, the first whose `when` holds is said (`when` may hold `deed` (a match against any deed this world), `met`, `with` or `fallen`, each a hero id, and `not`, any of those that must not hold). A line's `speaker` is `{owner}` (whose arc it is) or `{listener}` (who they are talking to). A deed match is `kind`, and `told` the start of how it is said. `reward`: `marks` added to the owner for good (`attack`, `defense`, `max_hp`), `bond` warmth with whoever listened, and `annal`, written in the annals. Started with one lead, Bellona, to find the shape (the issue's word); `dougie` kept the shape and the other fifteen were written the same way (D256, issue #326). A stage's `until` and `skip_if` may also ask (D256): `ledger`, tallies grown since the stage opened (any of the run's counters, such as `battles_won`, `battles_lost`, `kills`, `errands_done`, `recruited`, plus `places`, places walked, and `one_kind`, the most of one kind of foe put down; `skip_if` counts them from nothing); `floor`, a Tower floor stood on; `flag`, a flag set (or any of a list); `met_count`, how many of the sixteen met. A line's `when` may also hold `fallen_count` (at least that many of the sixteen fallen) and `flag`. Bellona's lines and numbers are **Inferred** (agenda row 163), the other fifteen's (agenda row 168).

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a courtyard. Somebody put Sky's reins in my hands and said she was mine. I was too small to hold them.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Who was it?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I don't know. I know how the story ends, mostly. Not that part. Let Sky carry me through a few fights, and take me up to the sixth floor. The next page is there.

stages.ask: Win three fights with Sky carrying him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Three. She never once looked back to see if I was still on. Whoever gave her to me knew she wouldn't.

stages.ask: Climb with him to the Tower's sixth floor.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The sixth floor. I thought the page would tell me who gave her to me. It tells me what happens to the sixteen at the top instead.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: And one of us has already fallen. The story I read had sixteen in it. It's wrong now, and I'm glad. Wrong means it can change.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Is that good?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: It's the only good thing I've read.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The sixth floor. Sky put her head down by the stair and wouldn't go on until I patted her. She's done that before, somewhere.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I still don't know who gave her to me. I know they meant me to get this far. That will do for now.

reward.line: Atlas sits Sky a little easier: +1 attack, for good. The Gift.
reward.annal: Atlas rode Sky up to the sixth floor and did not look back to see if she would follow.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a door I slept against. I'd promised somebody I'd get up for the hard ones.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: And this is one?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Not yet. A gate nobody understands would be. Shut one with me. Then the eighth floor: there's a hall up there full of doors, and I think one is mine.

stages.ask: Shut a gate with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: You've shut one already without me. Fine. I'll count it. I'd have slept through it anyway.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: That was hard. I stayed up for all of it. I'd forgotten I could.

stages.ask: Climb with him to the eighth floor, the hall of shut doors.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The doors on the eighth floor. Sixteen of them. One stands open.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: A door opens when one of us dies. I didn't know that until I saw it. I'd rather not have.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Do you know whose?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: No. I'm going to find out. That's a hard one. I'll get up for it.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The doors on the eighth floor, all shut. Sixteen. I sat against one, like I used to.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I didn't sleep. First time. I think that was the promise.

reward.line: Janus stays awake for it now: +4 health, for good. The Hard Ones.
reward.annal: Janus sat against a shut door on the eighth floor and did not sleep.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a gate. On the fifth floor, in a dent in a whistle. I shut it with people still on the road outside, and I'd do it again.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: And down here we've already left someone on a road. No wall, no order. We just kept walking.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: So what do you want to do about it?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Give someone their twenty. Then shut a gate and look over the wall first. Humour me.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a gate. On the fifth floor, in a dent in a whistle. I shut it with people still on the road outside, and I'd do it again.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Would you?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Yes. But I'd like there to be a road somewhere I didn't shut. Give someone their twenty, then a gate, and I look over the wall first. Humour me.

stages.ask: Give somebody on the road their twenty: stop for them, see them home, or hold a town that is attacked.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We've stopped for people on the road before. I saw. That's the twenty, then. A gate's left.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: You stopped for them. Good. That's one I didn't count out.

stages.ask: Shut a gate with her, and let her look over the wall first.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I looked over the wall before it went dark. Nobody there.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: And I thought of a boy. I don't know his face. One of us called Ultor fell, in a world that ended, and that's the name that came. I don't know why it hurts.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Maybe you knew him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Maybe I owed him. I'll never know which now.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Ultor watched me the whole time we were in there. As if he was waiting to see if I'd look over the wall.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I did, this time. I don't know what he is to me. I think he does.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I looked over the wall before it went dark. Nobody there.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: There's one of us out there, Ultor. When we met he looked at me like I owed him something. I think I do. I don't know what yet.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We burned a town, and now we've shut a gate and called it good. I know how that sum comes out. I've done it before, above.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: And I'll carry it. That's what a wall is for.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I looked over the wall before it went dark. Nobody there. Nobody left outside.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll take it. Thank you for humouring me.

reward.line: Bellona stands a little squarer: +2 guard, for good. The Last Wall.
reward.annal: Bellona looked over the wall before the gate went dark, and nobody was left outside.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a festival. There was a mask nobody wanted, and I asked for it. Somebody had to play the monster so somebody else could play the hero.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: And now?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Now I'd like to know what it's like from the other side. Lose a fight with me and get up again. Then take me to the arena, where a crowd picks a hero, and let's see who they boo.

stages.ask: Lose a fight with him, and live.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: There. That's what the monster feels at the end of the play. You get up and nobody claps. It's not so bad.

stages.ask: Win the arena tournament with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: They cheered. For us. I kept waiting for somebody to step out of the crowd and take the part off me.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: There was one of us I think would have. Cassius, the monster, Caesar, the hero. He fell, and I never shook his hand.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: You knew him?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I knew his part. I played the other half of it. That's all I'll ever know now.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Caesar cheered loudest. As if it was his to give.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: He keeps looking at me as if we've met. Perhaps we did, in masks. I'm not going to make it easy for him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: They cheered. I didn't know where to put my hands.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: There's one of us out there called Caesar, the kind a crowd picks. When we met he held his hand out to me as if he owed it. I didn't take it. I might, next time.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: They cheered. For us. For about a minute I wasn't anybody's monster.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Then I remembered I chose it, and I'd choose it again. But a minute's nice.

reward.line: Cassius takes the next hit a little better: +1 guard and +2 health, for good. The Monster's Part.
reward.annal: Cassius won the arena, and for a minute was nobody's monster.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a table I laid for everyone, and a place that stayed empty. I still set it, in my head, every time we eat.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Whose was it?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I don't know. Bring someone new to our table, then find us a house, a whole one, in Stormreach. I want a table with room.

stages.ask: Take somebody new into the company.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Another one at the fire. Good. I'll set a place they don't have to ask for.

stages.ask: Buy the narrow house in Stormreach, a table with room.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: A house, a table, and every place set. One of the sixteen has fallen, and I set theirs too. I always will.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Even not knowing who they were to you?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: That's why. A place doesn't ask.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We burned a town on the way here. I set a place for them as well. It doesn't fix it. It's what I have.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: A house, a table, every place set. One is still empty. I don't mind it as much as I did.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Thank you. Sit. There's room.

reward.line: Saturn eats as well as feeds: +5 health, for good. The Empty Place.
reward.annal: Saturn laid a table in Stormreach with every place set, and one left for whoever was missing.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered the last fire in a house everyone left. They went back through a door to how things were. I stayed.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: You want a fire to keep.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: One that stays lit when we leave it. Have Muck Muck build the infirmary at the crater, and I'll keep its hearth. Then let my fire do its work: twelve of what we fight.

stages.ask: Have the crater's infirmary built, for her to keep its hearth.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The infirmary at the crater has a hearth already. Nobody's keeping it. I will.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Ness keeps the beds. I'll keep the fire. It'll be lit when we come back. That's the whole of it.

stages.ask: Put down twelve foes with her.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Twelve. My fire took them clean. It only burns what's dead already.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: One of the sixteen fell. I lit a fire for them at the crater, and I'll keep it. Somebody has to stay.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: You're not going back either, are you.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: No. Back was never back.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Twelve. My fire only burns the dead, and it burned them.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The hearth at the crater is lit. I'll keep it if everyone else leaves. I'd like it if you didn't.

reward.line: Vesta's fire burns a little hotter: +1 attack, for good. The One Fire.
reward.annal: Vesta lit a hearth at the crater and said she would keep it if everyone else left.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a festival. I played the hero and everybody cheered. Somebody played the monster so I could, and I never asked who.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: So be a hero.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: That's the easy half. Hold a town when it's attacked, where nobody's cheering. Then five fights, and I get back up after every one.

stages.ask: Hold a town that is attacked.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We held a town already. Nobody cheered. That's how it should be, I think.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Nobody cheered. They just went back in and shut their doors. That's the real part, isn't it.

stages.ask: Win five fights with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Five. I kept getting up. And I thought about the monster at the festival.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: One of us called Cassius fell. The name came with the mask. I'll never get to ask him.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Ask him what?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Why he took it. So I could be the hero. I never even said thank you.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Cassius watched every fight like he was waiting for me to fall off a stage.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I didn't. I'm going to ask him one day what part he thinks I owe him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Five. And there's one of us out there, Cassius, who wouldn't take my hand when we met.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I think he played something for me once. I'll find out what.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We burned a town. Heroes don't. I know that's the festival talking. I'll carry it anyway.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Five, and I got up every time. Nobody cheered. I liked it better.

reward.line: Caesar gets up quicker: +1 attack and +2 health, for good. The Hero's Part.
reward.annal: Caesar held a town where nobody cheered, and liked it better.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a game. The last moment, and the shot was mine, and I passed. We lost.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Next time?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Next time I take it. Carry somebody home for me, that's the pass, I'm good at that. Then the shot: a bounty, and I want to be the one who claims it.

stages.ask: See somebody safely into a town.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We've seen somebody home already. That's the pass made. Now the shot.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: That's the pass. I could do that all day. Now the hard bit.

stages.ask: Claim a bounty from the board.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I took it. Nobody to pass to, and I didn't look for anyone.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: One of the sixteen has fallen. I keep thinking I'd have passed to them. Now I can't, so I'll take every shot I'm given.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I took it. And it went in. Just like that.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: How does it feel?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Like I've been running the wrong way all my life. I'll pass again. Just not every time.

reward.line: Iris takes the shot now: +2 attack, for good. Take the Shot.
reward.annal: Iris claimed a bounty herself and passed it to nobody.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered standing at the top of a stair, alone, counting the ones who climbed with me. None of them made it.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: What do you want?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: To count properly. Ten of one kind of thing, put down, one at a time. Then the seventh floor. And this time nobody pays but me.

stages.ask: Put down ten of one kind of foe with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Ten. I know how they move now. That's what counting's for.

stages.ask: Climb with him to the seventh floor.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The seventh floor. I counted us up the stair. One of the sixteen is missing from the count.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I said nobody pays but me. I was wrong already.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: It wasn't you.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: It's always the one counting.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The seventh floor. I counted us up the stair, and everyone's here.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll count again at the next one. I always will. Thank you for being there to count.

reward.line: Pluto's count is steadier: +1 attack and +1 guard, for good. One at a Time.
reward.annal: Pluto counted the company up the stair to the seventh floor, one at a time.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a granary full of children who weren't mine, and something walking the fields, and sitting on the lid all night.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Did you keep them?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I don't know how many. Pull somebody off the road for me. Then get Muck Muck to put a wall round the crater, so there's a lid on something.

stages.ask: Pull somebody off the road.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We've pulled somebody off the road already. One kept. Good.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: One kept. I'll stop counting there. Counting's how you lose them.

stages.ask: Have the crater's wall built.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: There's a wall round the crater now. And we let someone on the road go by.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I keep thinking of them outside it. I won't do that again.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: A wall round the crater. And we burned a town. I'd like to forget which one. I won't.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: A wall round the crater, and everyone inside it.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: All of them?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: All of them. This time.

reward.line: Ceres sits a little heavier on the lid: +6 health, for good. Keep Them All.
reward.annal: Ceres saw a wall go round the crater, with everyone inside it.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a list I wrote for if it went wrong. The first rule was find the others. Somebody wiped the last line.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: So we find the others.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: By the book. Two errands off a board first, done properly. Then two of the sixteen found and met. I'll write them down.

stages.ask: Finish two errands from a job board.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Two, done and paid. Rules keep you alive. Now the first one on the list.

stages.ask: Meet two of the sixteen.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Two found and written down. There was one name I'd have put first. Ultor. I don't know why.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: He's fallen. I'll write him anyway. Somebody wanted him left off once. Not on my list.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Two found, and Ultor with us. I wrote him down first. I don't know why I needed to.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Does he know?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: He doesn't need to. It's my list.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Two of us found and written down. The last line's still gone.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: That's two more than I had. Rules keep you alive. So does company.

reward.line: Cato's list holds: +2 guard, for good. The First Rule.
reward.annal: Cato found two of the sixteen and wrote them down, by the book.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a cold room and an old cook who gave me the last of the pot and said he'd eaten. He hadn't.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: And you want to feed people.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I want a table. Take the room at the Flagon, so there's somewhere to sit. Then find me four of the sixteen. Everyone passes my table sooner or later.

stages.ask: Take the Flagon's room in Stormreach.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We've a room in Stormreach already. Good. A table's a table.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: A room, a table, a pot. Nobody at it goes hungry. Not even you.

stages.ask: Meet four of the sixteen.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Four of us, at my table, near enough. And one of the sixteen fallen. I'd have known where they were last seen.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll keep a plate for them. And I'll say I've eaten.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Have you?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Four of us met, and I know where they're all headed. That's what a table's for.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Eat. I already have.

reward.line: Juno eats her share, for once: +4 health, for good. A Table Everyone Passes.
reward.annal: Juno kept a table in Stormreach that four of the sixteen passed.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a road, a gate and a whistle. Somebody threw me under the gate and stayed outside.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: And you'll find them.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll know the whistle. Until then I get stronger. Twenty of what we fight. Then a gate shut, and I'm on the right side of it this time.

stages.ask: Put down twenty foes with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Twenty. That's the getting stronger. Now the gate.

stages.ask: Shut a gate with him, on the right side of it.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The gate came down and I was inside. I listened for a whistle the whole time.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Bellona's fallen. One of us. I don't know why her name stopped me on the stair.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Maybe she's the one.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Then I'll never know which of us owed the other.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Bellona looked over the wall before it shut. Like she was counting.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I've heard her whistle at drill. I don't know why I can't stop listening to it.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Shut, with me inside. There's one of us out there, Bellona, who blows a whistle at her people like a gate's coming down.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll know it, when I'm sure.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Shut, with me on the right side. I chose you for it. That's what I do: I choose a captain.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Don't make me sorry.

reward.line: Ultor has chosen his captain: +2 attack, for good. The Whistle.
reward.annal: Ultor shut a gate from the right side of it, with the captain he chose.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered a hill, and a village that feared it, and a wolf that let them think it was me. To keep them away from me.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Do you mind?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I don't know. Fight a band off the road beside the Watch, where people can see who does the killing. Then the ninth floor. There's something of mine there.

stages.ask: Fight a band off the road beside the Watch.

deeds.told: fought a band off the road beside the Watch
fought a band off the road beside the Watch

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: We've fought beside the Watch already. They saw. They'll still say it was the wolf.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: They saw. They'll still say it was the wolf. Let them.

stages.ask: Climb with her to the ninth floor.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The ninth floor. And we burned a town on the way. Now they're right to be afraid of me.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'd rather they were wrong.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The ninth floor, and a town we held behind us. They'll say the wolf did that too.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Will you tell them?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: No. It kept them away from me. It kept them safe. That's the same thing.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: The ninth floor. I wasn't afraid on the stair. I was small once, and I wasn't afraid then either.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'd forgotten.

reward.line: Diana stands her ground: +1 attack and +1 guard, for good. Who Does the Killing.
reward.annal: Diana climbed to the ninth floor and was not afraid on the stair.

ares.title: Ares's: Put It on My Name

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered teaching somebody small to fight, and a cut rope on the yard gate, and lying for him. I was glad.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Who was he?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Don't know. So let's teach somebody else. Take on somebody new, and I'll show them. Then the arena, and everybody hears my name.

stages.ask: Take somebody new into the company, for him to teach.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: New one. Holds a blade like it's hot. Good. That's how I held it.

stages.ask: Win the arena tournament with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Won. They shouted my name. I wanted to hear somebody else's.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Liber. One of us, fell. That's the name that came. I lied for somebody once. I'd lie for him.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: You don't know it was him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I know I'd have been glad.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Won, and Liber shouting louder than the crowd. Fights like I taught him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I didn't. Did I?

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Won. And there's one of us out there, Liber, who looked at me like I'd done him a favour.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Put it on my name, whatever it was.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Won! Put it on my name. All of it. The good and the lies.

reward.line: Ares lasts past his first ten seconds now: +1 attack and +3 health, for good. Put It on My Name.
reward.annal: Ares won the arena and wished they had shouted somebody else's name.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I remembered cutting a rope on a gate and running. Somebody let me go and took the blame.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: And you'd like to thank them.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'd like to pay it on. Cut somebody loose: pull them off the road. Then let's go, everywhere: eight places, never the same twice.

stages.ask: Pull somebody off the road.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Cut loose. They ran and didn't look back. Good. That's how you do it.

stages.ask: Walk eight places with him.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Eight places. I looked for a big man in every one. Ares, his name came to me. He's fallen.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I wanted to say thank you. I never stay long enough to say anything.

lines.speaker: {listener}
lines.text: Say it now.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Thank you. There.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Eight places, and Ares in every one of them, laughing. He wraps my hands before a fight. I never asked him to.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll say thank you properly one day.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Eight places. In one of them there was Ares, who looked at me as if I owed him for something. I think I do.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: I'll find him again and pay it.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: Eight places, never the same twice. That's freedom. I'd like to share it with whoever let me go.

lines.speaker: {owner}
lines.text: You'll do for now.

reward.line: Liber hits like he's free: +1 attack and +2 health, for good. The Cut Rope.
reward.annal: Liber walked eight places and stayed in none of them, and said thank you to someone at last.
